sources.title: State of London
sources.verified_claim: The 2026 State of London report records 75,800 homeless households in temporary accommodation at September 2025 and continued housing-cost pressure. London-level pressure is not a parcel-specific demand forecast.

sources.title: Private rent and house prices, UK: July 2026
sources.verified_claim: ONS reports average London private rent of £2,302 in June 2026 and 2.2% annual rent inflation, with recent estimates subject to revision. Regional rent statistics are not exact parcel rental-demand evidence.

sources.title: London Living Rent
sources.verified_claim: City Hall states the 2026-27 average two-bedroom London Living Rent is around £1,409 per month against an average market rent reference of £2,168 in December 2025. Benchmark affordability does not establish a sample parcel's achievable rent or tenure.

sources.title: Services for people experiencing homelessness, including sleeping rough
sources.verified_claim: City Hall describes the Rough Sleeping Plan of Action, pan-London services and 2026 extreme-heat guidance. Service capacity and programme spending are homelessness-response context, not development demand at the sample parcels.

sources.title: ADD2820 Extensions to pan-London Rough Sleeping Accommodation Programme services for 2026-27
sources.verified_claim: ADD2820 extends specified pan-London RSAP services through March 2027 and reallocates funding during a grant transition. Programme continuity is not a parcel housing-delivery award.

sources.title: Homelessness
sources.verified_claim: Enfield states there is a severe lack of affordable rental homes and that emergency or rented housing offers may be outside the borough or London. Local housing pressure is retained as context, not proof of parcel demand or viability.

sources.title: Housing user guides, policies and strategies
sources.verified_claim: Havering's current policy index lists a 2025 Temporary Accommodation Placement Policy and also lists a Homelessness Strategy whose stated period is 2020-2025. The expired strategy period is retained and not silently treated as current strategy content.

sources.title: London homelessness charity welcomes Lambeth’s new strategy to tackle rough sleeping
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth reports implementation of its new homelessness and rough-sleeping strategy with partnership outreach and prevention priorities. Strategy adoption and service activity do not establish development demand at parcel_61522.
